transport.name: TECO Line Streetcar
transport.operator: HART, under contract to Tampa Historic Streetcar, Inc.
transport.fare_text: Free: all rides are fare free.
transport.hours_text: Every 15 minutes. Mon-Thu 7:00 AM-11:00 PM; Fri 7:00 AM-2:00 AM; Sat 9:00 AM-2:00 AM; Sun 8:30 AM-11:00 PM. Runs until midnight Sun-Thu when there is a Lightning game or evening event at Benchmark International Arena.
transport.summary: A free electric heritage streetcar on a 2.7-mile line with 11 covered, wheelchair-accessible stations linking downtown Tampa, the Channel District and Ybor City; an end-to-end trip takes about 25 minutes. Pull the overhead cord to request your stop; bikes are not allowed on board.

transport.notes: Stop coordinates are HART's own (GTFS feed version 2608.4, stops.txt, route 800), i.e. operator-published. Service change effective June 22, 2025: a consistent 15-minute frequency 7 days a week (12-minute peak service discontinued). Pets: service dogs; non-service dogs in small carriers. Extension: the City of Tampa's InVision: Tampa Streetcar page describes a preferred alternative with modern vehicles and a 1.3-mile extension from the western end through downtown to Tampa Heights, in project development; the page gives no construction or opening date, so nothing is scheduled as far as the pages read show. A rider alert on the home page (Sant' Yago Knight Parade) is event-specific and not recorded. The How to Ride page still lists Coast Bike Share among connections; see the bike-share record. Verified 2026-09-27: operator home, How to Ride and About pages re-read; fare, hours, stations, 25-minute running time, extended arena-night service and rules all match; the city's InVision page (updated 06/04/2026) still gives no construction date.

transport.name: Pirate Water Taxi
transport.fare_text: All-Day Pass: adult $34, child (ages 2-12) $24; Annual Membership $199.95. Cashless on the boat; tickets online or at the booth at Stop 7.
transport.hours_text: Mon-Thu 11:30 AM-6:30 PM; Fri-Sun 11:30 AM-9:30 PM. On weekdays boats leave Stop 7 toward Stop 16 at 11:30 AM, 1:00, 2:30, 4:00 and 5:30 PM; departures are more frequent Friday-Sunday.
transport.summary: A hop-on, hop-off water taxi on the Hillsborough River and the Channel District waterfront with 10 numbered stops from the Florida Aquarium to Armature Works; an all-day pass covers unlimited rides. Boats are covered and wheelchair accessible, though not every dock is; bikes and luggage are not allowed on board, and service stops for lightning, heavy rain and high winds.

Stop 15: Julian B. Lane Riverfront Park
Stop 3: Benchmark International Arena / Tampa History Center
Stop 2: Sparkman Wharf / Yacht StarShip / Craft
Stop 1: Florida Aquarium / American Victory Ship

transport.notes: Same service as the exp-water experience pirate-water-taxi (kept under a separate id here because this is the transport record). Stops are listed in the order the schedule serves them (7, 8, 11, 12, 15, 16, then 4, 3, 2, 1 and back to 7). Stop coordinates are the named landmark (the place records' points: census or OpenStreetMap), not the dock itself; Stop 11 (Arabelle Riverwalk) and Stop 4 (Harbour Island) have no point because no source placed the dock. The map page says route schedule and stop availability may be affected by low or high tides. FAQ: no reservations needed (first-come, first-served); children 13 and under must ride with someone 14 or older; the boats do not go to St. Pete; the zoo route was discontinued in 2017; parking is not included (the FAQ suggests the Tampa Convention Center, Pam Iorio and Fort Brooke garages). Verified 2026-09-27: schedule, rates ($34/$24, annual $199.95), FAQ and map pages re-read; all match. Stop 1's point was corrected to the florida-aquarium place point (the earlier point sat about 220 m west, at Sparkman Wharf). The site also advertises a Rain Day Guarantee (if rain stops service for more than 90 minutes, you may return the next day) and live-tracking links for a 'River Route' and an 'Island Loop'.

transport.name: DASH (Downtown Area Shared Hubs)
transport.fare_text: $2 per person, requested and paid through the DASH Tampa app.
transport.hours_text: Mon-Sat 7 AM-11 PM; Sun 12 PM-9 PM.
transport.summary: An app-hailed, hub-to-hub ride service in downtown Tampa using all-electric vehicles, with more than twenty virtual hubs; each ride costs $2 per person. Wheelchair-accessible rides are provided by partner Wheelchair Transport Service (813-540-3333).
transport.notes: DASH drivers are part of the Partnership's Downtown Ambassadors team. The Partnership says hubs may be adjusted and the app has day-to-day changes. The Tampa Downtown Partnership page links the rider app 'DASH Tampa Microtransit' (package com.ridewithvia.dashtamparider); Visit Tampa Bay's page still links an older app listing. The Downtowner name no longer appears on these Tampa pages; no page read describes a Downtowner service in St. Pete or Clearwater in 2026 (not verified either way). Verified 2026-09-27: DASH page re-read; fare, hours, hubs and accessibility partner match.

transport.name: Shared e-scooters and e-bikes (Tampa)
transport.operator: Lime and Spin, under the City of Tampa Shared Micromobility Program
transport.summary: Lime and Spin rent e-scooters and e-bikes across the City of Tampa through their apps; riders must be 16 or older with a valid driver's license or permit, and helmets are encouraged but not required. The city bars them from the Tampa Riverwalk, Bayshore Boulevard and 7th Avenue in Ybor City, and asks riders to park upright in designated corrals.
transport.notes: City page (updated 05/07/2025) names two vendors, Lime (www.li.me, 1-888-LIME-345) and Spin (www.spin.app, 1-888-262-5189); vehicles travel up to about 15 mph and 15-20 miles per charge. Fares are set in the vendors' apps and are not on the city page. Visit Tampa Bay's transportation page also names Bird; the city page does not, so Bird is not listed here. The page's '7th Avenue' is read as Ybor City's 7th Avenue (the page does not say which). Verified 2026-09-27: city page (updated 05/07/2025) re-read; rules match.

transport.fare_text: Free.
transport.hours_text: Daily. Eastbound from Grand Central Station every 30 minutes, 6:33 AM-9:33 PM; westbound from 2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive 6:14 AM-9:39 PM (last arrival 10:01 PM).
transport.summary: A free PSTA trolley along Central Avenue between Grand Central Station and the St. Pete Pier (2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive), running every 30 minutes daily.

transport.name: HART buses
transport.fare_text: Local and Limited Express: $2.00 a trip, capped at $4.00 a day and $65.00 a month when you pay with the Flamingo Fares app or card, a contactless bank card or a phone wallet. Discount fare $1.00 (cap $2.00 a day). 1 Day Family Pass $12.50 (up to 5 people, Flamingo app only). 3-Day Visitor Pass $11.75 (sold only at select HART facilities and hotels). Month Passport $85.00 (HART and PSTA). HARTFlex $1.00. Children 5 and under ride free with a paying adult.
transport.hours_text: Varies by route; routes 10, 30 and 32 serve Tampa International Airport seven days a week.
transport.summary: Hillsborough County's bus system, with local routes, limited-express commuter routes and HARTFlex, meeting at the Marion Transit Center downtown. Routes 10 (Cypress St.) and 30 (Kennedy Blvd./Town 'N Country) link downtown Tampa with the Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center, reached from the terminal by the SkyConnect train.

stops.name: Marion Transit Center, 1211 N Marion St (downtown hub; Greyhound/FlixBus; PSTA 100 and 300)
Tampa International Airport Rental Car Center (routes 10, 30, 32; PSTA 300)

HART's bus page says routes 10, 30 and 32 can be picked up near the Rental Car Center (take SkyConnect from the Red Baggage Claim); the same page also still describes the In-Towner (Route 96) and names Amalie Arena, so parts of it are dated and its hours for routes 10/30 are not repeated here. The schedule book effective Aug 16, 2026 lists Route 30 (Kennedy Blvd./Town 'N Country, via the airport to the Northwest Transfer Center) and Route 10 (Cypress St.) to the Rental Car Center; Route 32 (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd.) runs from the Netpark Transfer Center to the airport. The schedules page also lists MetroRapid (Downtown Tampa to UATC/Hidden River Park-n-Ride via Nebraska Ave.). Stop coordinates are from HART's GTFS stops.txt (feed 2608.4). HARTInfo line: 813-254-4278. Verified 2026-09-27: fares page re-read (3-Day Visitor Pass and the under-5 rule added). The bus page's hidden airport block says routes 10, 30 and 32 'can be picked up near the Rental Car Center. Take the Airport's SkyConnect from the Red Baggage Claim to the Rental Car Center'; Route 10 weekday service 5:30 a.m. to midnight, weekends 7 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. (bus page). Schedule book pages 22-24 (Route 10) and 39-41 (Route 30, Downtown Tampa to Tampa Airport to Northwest) confirm the airport routes.

transport.name: PSTA buses
transport.fare_text: $2.25 a ride; with Flamingo Fares or tap-to-pay the most you pay is $5 a day and $85 a calendar month. Reduced fare $1.10 (cap $2.50 a day). Cash (exact change, no pennies) is accepted on all routes except the SunRunner, without fare caps. Children 8 and under ride free. 1 Day Flamingo Fares Group Pass $5 for up to 4 people.
transport.summary: Pinellas County's transit agency: fixed-route buses, the SunRunner rapid bus, the Suncoast Beach Trolley along the Gulf beaches, and express routes 100 and 300 to downtown Tampa. Tap a contactless card (not American Express), Apple Pay, Google Pay or the Flamingo Fares app to get the daily and monthly fare caps.
transport.notes: PSTA's own description (press releases, 2026): 41 fixed-route bus routes, two express routes to downtown Tampa, the Suncoast Beach Trolley, the Jolley Trolley and the Looper, and 10.7 million rides a year. US military veterans ride free with a PSTA veterans pass (fares page). Customer information: (727) 540-1900 (per the Looper site). The PSTA site listed many route detours on Sep 27, 2026; they are not recorded. Verified 2026-09-27: fares page re-read; all amounts match.

transport.name: SunRunner
transport.fare_text: Same as regular PSTA service: $2.25 a ride (reduced fares available). Cashless: tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard or Discover card, phone or watch, or use Flamingo Fares; American Express and cash are not accepted.
transport.hours_text: Seven days a week, 6 AM to midnight. Every 15 minutes until 8 PM, then every 30 minutes until midnight; every 15 minutes until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays (SunRunner After Dark).
transport.summary: Tampa Bay's first bus rapid transit line, a 10-mile, 16-stop route with dedicated bus lanes between downtown St. Petersburg and St. Pete Beach via the Grand Central and EDGE districts and South Pasadena; PSTA says the trip takes about 35 minutes. Buses have level boarding, three interior bike racks, free Wi-Fi and charging at every seat.
transport.notes: PSTA lists destinations served: downtown St. Petersburg, USF St. Pete, Tropicana Field, TradeWinds Island Resort, the Grand Central and EDGE business districts, Bayfront, Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, South Pasadena and St. Pete Beach. The page says 31 stations (both directions) and a 10-mile, 16-stop line; station names and points were not published in the pages read, so stops are the three areas only. Rental bikes and scooters and tandem bikes are not allowed on board; small pets in carriers are. The page links bike share at gohopr.com/coast, which now says Coast Bike Share has closed (see the bike-share records). Verified 2026-09-27: service page re-read; hours, frequency, SunRunner After Dark, 10-mile 16-stop line, 35 minutes, cashless, no American Express all match.

transport.name: Downtown Looper
transport.operator: The Looper Group, Inc. (funded in part by PSTA)
transport.fare_text: Free.
transport.hours_text: Mon-Fri 7:00 AM-10:00 PM; Sat-Sun 8:00 AM-10:00 PM; every 15-20 minutes. Not running on Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
transport.summary: A free trolley loop around downtown St. Petersburg every 15-20 minutes, stopping at the Vinoy, St. Pete City Hall, the SouthCore garage, Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, USF St. Petersburg, the Dali Museum (during museum hours only), the Mahaffey Theater, the James Museum, the Sundial garage and the St. Pete Pier. All trolleys have a wheelchair lift; PSTA's Central Avenue Trolley connects with it on Bayshore Drive near the Pier approach.

Park Street Terminal (Garden Ave and Park St, downtown Clearwater)

transport.notes: The route page lists: St. Pete Beach, 75th Ave and Gulf Blvd, Treasure Island, John's Pass Village, Madeira Beach, Redington Beach, North Redington Beach, Redington Shores, Park Blvd Boat Ramp, Indian Shores, Indian Rocks Beach, Bay Park, Clearwater Sailing Center, Sand Key, Pier 60, Clearwater Beach, Mandalay Park, Island Estates (intermittent) and Park Street Terminal. The route page does not state a fare; Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page gives '$2.25 per ride', matching PSTA's fares page. Transit-center points are OpenStreetMap bus stops. transport.name: Jolley Trolley

Per PSTA's posted timetables: North Beach Route 9:41 AM-10:01 PM Sunday-Thursday and until about 11:51 PM Friday-Saturday; South Beach Route 9:48 AM-10:10 PM Sunday-Thursday; Coastal Route first northbound trip 8:21 AM from Dunedin (Main St and Pinellas Trail), with the last trips reaching downtown Clearwater at 9:27 PM Sunday-Thursday and 12:27 AM Friday-Saturday.
transport.summary: Trolleys on Clearwater Beach (North Beach and South Beach routes around the beach, Island Estates and Sand Key, as far south as Bay Park) and a Coastal Route from Clearwater Beach and downtown Clearwater to Dunedin, Palm Harbor and the Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks. The fare is $2.25; the trolleys carry two bikes on a front rack and do not go to John's Pass.

Gulf Blvd and Bayside Gardens (Sand Key)
Safford St and Tarpon Ave (Tarpon Springs)

Coastal Route stops on the operator's list: Beach Transit Center, Clearwater Beach Marina, Park Street (PSTA), Osceola/Cleveland St, Dunedin, Curlew, Ozona (Friday evening-Sunday), Florida Avenue, Alderman, E Tarpon Avenue, Rusty Bellies. transport.fare_text: $2.25 cash fare (exact change; drivers carry no change), reduced $1.10, children 8 and under free; contactless payment and group passes through Flamingo Fares. Guests of the Sandpearl, Opal Sands, Sheraton Sand Key, Marriott Sand Key and TradeWinds ride free with their room card (plus four guests).

transport.name: Grouper Airport Express (PIE to Clearwater Beach)
transport.fare_text: One-way: $8 single rider (seniors 65+ $4); $20 total for groups of 3-4; $30 total for groups of 5-8. The airport's own page lists higher fares ($10 single, $30 for four, $40 for five to eight).
transport.hours_text: Every day and time the airport has inbound or outbound flights; book on demand or up to 2 months ahead.
transport.summary: A shared, bookable shuttle between St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport (PIE) and any address on Clearwater Beach, including the Sheraton and Marriott Sand Key resorts; book through grouper.psta.net or the Grouper app. At PIE the pickup is through the west baggage claim exit doors; drivers help with luggage and the service is wheelchair accessible.

stops.name: St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport, west baggage claim exit
Any location on Clearwater Beach (including Sand Key resorts)

transport.notes: Fare conflict: PSTA's Grouper page and the City of Clearwater page say $8/$20/$30; PIE's transportation page says 'Fares begin at $10 for single riders, $30 for group of four, and $40 for groups of five to eight.' The verifier should check which is current. Rides must start and end at PIE or Clearwater Beach; no service within Clearwater Beach or to other Tampa Bay places. Some rides are provided by taxi. Booking needs the web booker or app and a phone that receives texts; no cancellation fees. The PIE point is the OpenStreetMap airfield, not the exit door. Verified 2026-09-27: PSTA and City of Clearwater still say $8/$20/$30; PIE's page still says 'Fares begin at $10'. PSTA operates the service, so its fares lead.

transport.name: Clearwater Ferry

The home page says fares rose by $1 effective Sep 17, 2026, so the sheet may predate the increase.

transport.summary: A passenger ferry linking downtown Clearwater (Coachman Park), the Clearwater Beach Marina near Pier 60 and the Dunedin Marina, so you can reach the beach without driving and parking. Reservations are recommended but not required; walk-ons board if there is room, and service can be suspended in bad weather.
transport.notes: Same service as the exp-water experience clearwater-ferry (separate id for the transport record). Stop points are OpenStreetMap ferry-terminal nodes named 'PSTA Clearwater Downtown Ferry Stop', 'PSTA Clearwater Beach Marina Ferry Stop' and 'PSTA Dunedin Marina Ferry Stop'. The schedule PDF shows Red Line departures on the hour from Downtown Clearwater (10:00 AM-8:00 PM) and on the half hour from Clearwater Beach Marina (10:30 AM-7:30 PM), and Blue Line trips every two hours; it carries no date. Weather/text line 727-643-1832. FAQ answers on the site load by script and could not be read. Verified 2026-09-27: home, schedule, getting-there pages and the schedule PDF re-read (headless browser). The Tickets & Fares page shows only the notice 'EFFECTIVE THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 17TH, 2026: PSTA's Clearwater Ferry fare prices will be increased by $1.'; the PDF's fares are undated, so both are given. The City of Clearwater says the Clearwater Beach Marina is being renovated (no transient docks).

transport.name: Tampa Bay Ferry (St. Petersburg-Tampa)
transport.season_text: Not running as of Sep 27, 2026. PSTA's Sep 24, 2026 budget release says the service 'is scheduled to launch later this year'; no start date, docks, fares or schedule are published.
transport.summary: There is no passenger ferry across the bay between downtown St. Petersburg and Tampa right now: PSTA is preparing a new Tampa Bay Ferry service to replace the former Cross-Bay Ferry, with two vessels (Bay Breeze and Clipper) being refurbished in Tarpon Springs and a permanent dock planned in downtown St. Petersburg.
transport.notes: PSTA press releases of June 22, Sep 4 and Sep 8, 2026. The June release says no launch date is confirmed and calls the old service 'the previous Cross-Bay Ferry model'; the Sep 4 release says PSTA will announce a start date once refurbishment is nearing completion. crossbayferry.com showed only a parked/consent page on Sep 27, 2026. PSTA also received a $16.5 million FTA grant to buy a new vessel. Same subject as the exp-water experience tampa-bay-ferry (opening-soon). No docks, fares or schedule are published, so none are recorded; the Looper and PSTA pages still name a 'Cross Bay Ferry at Port St. Pete' stop. Verified 2026-09-27: PSTA's Sep 24, 2026 release: 'The Tampa Bay Ferry service from downtown St. Petersburg to downtown Tampa is scheduled to launch later this year.' The St. Pete Pier's page says the ferry 'is currently not running but is anticipated to start again in Fall of 2026' and still links thecrossbayferry.com. Visit St. Pete/Clearwater's transportation page still describes a November-May Cross Bay Ferry (out of date).

transport.name: Tampa International Airport
transport.summary: Tampa's airport, about five miles west of downtown Tampa, has a central main terminal linked by automated shuttles to Airsides A, C, E and F. The SkyConnect train runs from the main terminal to the Economy Parking garage and the Rental Car Center, where the HART and PSTA bus stop is; Yellow Cab taxis wait outside baggage claim and charge a $40 flat rate to downtown Tampa and the cruise terminal.
transport.address: 4100 George J. Bean Parkway, Tampa, FL 33607

SkyConnect Rental Car Center Station (HART and PSTA bus platform)

Uber's own page says to follow the Blue Express Pickup signs and, with bags, to take the elevator from baggage claim to level 3.
transport.notes: Verified 2026-09-27 on the airport's Ground Transportation page (read in a headless browser). Drop-offs may be at any public access location including Ticketing, Baggage Claim or the SkyCenter One remote curbside. Uber notes the map and zones can change with construction and airport rules. The point is the airport, not the pickup zone.

transport.name: St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport
transport.fare_text: Parking (new rates effective 10/1/26): Long Term $2.00 first hour, $1.00 each additional 20 minutes, $16.00 daily maximum; Short Term $25.00 daily maximum; Economy $12.00 per day.
transport.summary: The airport on Roosevelt Blvd (SR 686), 4 miles north of St. Petersburg, served by Allegiant and Sun Country (domestic) and BermudAir (international), with nonstops to more than 60 cities. Rideshare pickup is in front of the terminal at Arrivals; taxis and shuttles wait in the Ground Transportation lot outside baggage claim; PSTA's Grouper runs to Clearwater Beach.
transport.notes: Airlines page (Sep 27, 2026): Allegiant and Sun Country (domestic), BermudAir (Anguilla, Turks and Caicos, Belize), plus casino charters. Parking is first-come, first-served (no reservations); Economy lots Key Lime (across Roosevelt Blvd on 46th Street) and Strawberry (Fairchild Drive, opens as needed) with free shuttles. faqs.q: How do I get from Tampa International Airport to downtown Tampa without a car?
faqs.a: HART Routes 10 (Cypress St.) and 30 (Kennedy Blvd.) run between the airport and downtown Tampa seven days a week, and Route 32 connects the airport with the Netpark Transfer Center. The buses stop at the airport's Rental Car Center: take the SkyConnect train from the main terminal. A HART ride costs $2.00. A Yellow Cab taxi to downtown Tampa or the cruise terminal is a $40 flat rate, and Lyft, Uber and Wridz pick up at the Red Express or Blue Express curbside, with a $5.00 airport fee added to the fare.

faqs.q: Is there a bus from Tampa International Airport to St. Petersburg or Pinellas County?
faqs.a: PSTA says its new 727 Airport Express, between nine stops in downtown St. Petersburg and Tampa International Airport, launches October 4, 2026 and will run daily from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. (fare not yet published). Until then, and on weekdays after, PSTA's Route 300 express stops at the airport's Rental Car Facility on its way between downtown Tampa and the Ulmerton Park and Ride in Largo, Monday through Friday only, for the regular $2.25 fare.

faqs.q: How do I get from St. Pete-Clearwater airport (PIE) to Clearwater Beach?
faqs.a: PSTA's Grouper Airport Express is a shared ride between PIE and any address on Clearwater Beach, including the Sand Key resorts, booked through grouper.psta.net or the Grouper app. PSTA lists fares of $8 for one rider, $20 for 3-4 people and $30 for 5-8; the airport's own page lists higher fares ($10, $30 and $40). The pickup at PIE is through the west baggage claim exit doors.

faqs.q: Where do Uber and Lyft pick up at St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport?
faqs.a: The airport says rideshare drivers drop off in front of the terminal at Departures and pick up in front of the terminal at Arrivals; taxis and shuttles are outside baggage claim in the Ground Transportation lot.

faqs.q: Is the TECO Line Streetcar free?
faqs.a: Yes. The operator says all TECO Line Streetcar rides are fare free. It runs every 15 minutes between downtown Tampa, the Channel District and Ybor City: Monday to Thursday 7 AM-11 PM, Friday 7 AM-2 AM, Saturday 9 AM-2 AM and Sunday 8:30 AM-11 PM, and until midnight Sunday-Thursday on nights with a Lightning game or event at Benchmark International Arena.

faqs.q: Can I bring a bike or my dog on the streetcar?
faqs.a: Bikes are not allowed on the TECO Line Streetcar. Service dogs may ride; other dogs must be in small carriers. Folded strollers are allowed, and every station has a ramp and every car is wheelchair accessible.

faqs.q: Is the Tampa streetcar being extended?
faqs.a: The City of Tampa has studied extending and modernizing the streetcar: its preferred plan adds a 1.3-mile line from the current western end through downtown to Tampa Heights and replaces the replica cars with modern streetcars. The city's project page gives no construction or opening date.

faqs.q: Is there a ferry between Tampa and St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: Not as of late September 2026. PSTA is preparing a new Tampa Bay Ferry between downtown St. Petersburg and downtown Tampa to replace the former Cross-Bay Ferry, with Hubbard's Marina as operator and two vessels being refurbished in Tarpon Springs. On September 24, 2026 PSTA said the service is scheduled to launch later this year; it has not announced a start date, fares or docks.

faqs.q: How much does the Pirate Water Taxi cost, and where do I board?
faqs.a: An all-day hop-on, hop-off pass costs $34 for adults and $24 for children 2-12 (prices can change). You can board at any of its 10 stops; the ticket booth is at Stop 7, on the Riverwalk between the Tampa Convention Center and the Marriott Water Street. The boats are cashless, and no reservation is needed.

faqs.q: When does the Pirate Water Taxi run?
faqs.a: Monday to Thursday 11:30 AM-6:30 PM and Friday to Sunday 11:30 AM-9:30 PM. Service stops for lightning, heavy rain and high winds, and the operator says tides can affect the route and stops.

faqs.q: What is DASH in downtown Tampa?
faqs.a: DASH (Downtown Area Shared Hubs) is an app-hailed ride service run by the Tampa Downtown Partnership between more than twenty virtual hubs downtown, in all-electric vehicles, for $2 per person. It runs Monday to Saturday 7 AM-11 PM and Sunday 12 PM-9 PM.

faqs.q: How do I get from downtown St. Petersburg to St. Pete Beach without a car?
faqs.a: Take PSTA's SunRunner, a rapid bus that runs every 15 minutes (every 30 minutes after 8 PM, except Friday and Saturday nights) from 6 AM to midnight daily; PSTA says the trip takes about 35 minutes. The fare is $2.25 and must be paid by tapping a card, phone or watch or with Flamingo Fares: cash is not accepted.

faqs.q: Are there free trolleys in downtown St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: Yes. The Downtown Looper is free and loops downtown every 15-20 minutes (weekdays 7 AM-10 PM, weekends 8 AM-10 PM), and PSTA's Central Avenue Trolley is free between Grand Central Station and the St. Pete Pier every 30 minutes.

faqs.q: Is there a bus along the Gulf beaches?
faqs.a: PSTA's Suncoast Beach Trolley runs daily along Gulf Boulevard from St. Pete Beach (75th Ave) through Treasure Island, John's Pass, Madeira Beach, the Redingtons, Indian Shores, Indian Rocks Beach and Sand Key to Clearwater Beach and downtown Clearwater's Park Street Terminal; the PSTA fare is $2.25. On Clearwater Beach itself, the Jolley Trolley ($2.25) runs North Beach and South Beach routes and a Coastal Route to Dunedin, Palm Harbor and Tarpon Springs.

faqs.q: Is there a boat to Clearwater Beach?
faqs.a: The Clearwater Ferry runs Thursday to Sunday between downtown Clearwater, the Clearwater Beach Marina near Pier 60 and the Dunedin Marina. Reservations are recommended but not required, and walk-ons board if there is room.

faqs.q: How much is parking on Clearwater Beach?
faqs.a: City lots cost $3.50 an hour with no time limit from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; on-street parking is $4.00 an hour with a 5-hour limit. Pay at pay-by-plate kiosks, with the ParkMobile app, or by texting CLEARWATER to 727563. Private garages set their own rates.

faqs.q: How much does parking cost at Fort De Soto, Sand Key and other Pinellas County beach parks?
faqs.a: Pinellas County's beaches page says a $6-a-day parking fee applies at Fort De Soto, Sand Key and Fred Howard parks. From December 1, 2026, beach parking at the county's parks becomes $3.50 an hour, capped at $12 a day, plus tax, and from October 1, 2026 an annual beach pass valid at those three parks costs $95. Fort De Soto is cashless: pay at a machine, with the Flowbird or ParkMobile app, or by text.

faqs.q: How much is parking in downtown Tampa?
faqs.a: City of Tampa garages charge $3 an hour up to $18 a day (Fort Brooke, W.F. Poe, Pam Iorio, Convention Center) or $2 an hour up to $14 a day (Twiggs, Centro Ybor, Palm Ave.). Downtown street meters are $4 for the first hour and $3 for each hour after. You can pay with the Passport, PayByPhone, ParkMobile or Flowbird apps.

faqs.q: Is parking free in Ybor City?
faqs.a: The first two hours are free in the City of Tampa's Ybor lots, then $2 an hour up to $14 a day; a $10 flat rate applies Friday and Saturday from 8 p.m. to 3 a.m. Ybor street meters charge $3 for the first hour and $2 after.

faqs.q: Do I need a SunPass to drive around Tampa Bay?
faqs.a: No, but it is cheaper. The Tampa-area toll roads on Florida's Turnpike list (Veterans Expressway, Suncoast Parkway, I-4 Connector, Selmon Expressway and the Sunshine Skyway Bridge) do not accept cash. With SunPass, or an accepted transponder such as E-ZPass, E-PASS or Peach Pass, you pay the lowest toll rate; without one, Toll-By-Plate photographs the plate and mails the owner an invoice with a $2.50 administrative fee. Florida's Turnpike says SunPass saves an average of 25%.

faqs.q: How do tolls work in a rental car?
faqs.a: Most rental companies bill tolls through their own programs, each with its own fees, so check your agreement. If you have a SunPass PRO or other portable transponder, add the rental car's plate and rental dates to your SunPass account and remove the transponder when you return the car. Toll-By-Plate is not available for rental cars.

faqs.q: Does E-ZPass work in Florida?
faqs.a: Yes. Florida's Turnpike lists E-ZPass among the transponders accepted in electronic toll lanes, along with SunPass, E-PASS, Peach Pass, NC Quick Pass and others.

faqs.q: How much is the Sunshine Skyway Bridge toll?
faqs.a: For a two-axle car, FDOT's rate sheet (effective April 12, 2026) lists $1.16 with SunPass and $1.62 by Toll-By-Plate at the bridge's toll plazas. Cash is not accepted.

faqs.q: Is there bike share or scooter share in Tampa?
faqs.a: Coast Bike Share says it has closed all its Tampa sites and no longer operates in Florida. The City of Tampa's shared program has Lime and Spin e-bikes and e-scooters, rented in their apps; riders must be 16 or older with a driver's license or permit, and they may not ride on the Tampa Riverwalk, Bayshore Boulevard or 7th Avenue.

faqs.q: Can I rent a bike or scooter in St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's bike share uses Lime e-bikes, which you must end at a designated hub, and Spin and Lime rent e-scooters. Riders must be 18 or older, may not ride on sidewalks, and may ride to the St. Pete Pier but not on it; scooter corrals are at the base of the Pier.

faqs.q: Can I take a train to Tampa?
faqs.a: Amtrak serves Tampa Union Station (601 North Nebraska Avenue) with the Floridian, which Amtrak describes as a temporary combination of the Capitol Limited and Silver Star running daily between Chicago and Miami via Washington, DC.

faqs.q: Does Brightline go to Tampa?
faqs.a: No. Brightline's website describes service between Miami and Orlando with stops in Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton and West Palm Beach, and names no Tampa station.

faqs.q: Where do Greyhound and FlixBus buses stop in Tampa?
faqs.a: At the Tampa Bus Station, 1315 N Marion St, at HART's Marion Transit Center downtown, and at the University of South Florida (Holly Drive at Lot 3D). RedCoach stops at 3801 USF Holly Drive.

faqs.q: Which cruise lines sail from Tampa, and where are the terminals?
faqs.a: Port Tampa Bay lists Carnival, Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Norwegian and Margaritaville at Sea. Its three terminals are in the Channel District: Terminal 2 at 651 Channelside Drive, Terminal 3 at 815 Channelside Drive and Terminal 6 at 1333 McKay Street. The port's parking garage is across the street from Terminal 3.

faqs.q: Can I store luggage before a cruise from Tampa?
faqs.a: Not at the terminals: Port Tampa Bay says security rules leave no place to store bags for early arrivals. The port says the Florida Aquarium, next to Terminal 2 at 701 Channelside Drive, stores luggage free when you buy a discounted admission ticket.

faqs.q: Is there a bus between downtown Tampa and downtown St. Petersburg?
faqs.a: PSTA's Route 100 express runs Monday to Friday between the Marion Transit Center in downtown Tampa and the St. Pete Pier area (2nd Ave NE and Beach Drive), with stops at Gateway Mall and Britton Plaza. It charges the regular $2.25 PSTA fare and does not run on weekends.

faqs.q: Is there one transit pass for both Tampa and Pinellas buses?
faqs.a: HART sells a Month Passport for $85.00 that is valid on HART local, limited express and HARTFlex service and on PSTA buses and trolleys. Both agencies also use Flamingo Fares, with daily fare caps ($4.00 on HART, $5 on PSTA).

faqs.q: How much does it cost to park at St. Pete-Clearwater International Airport?
faqs.a: From October 1, 2026, long-term parking is $2.00 for the first hour, $1.00 for each additional 20 minutes, up to $16.00 a day; short-term tops out at $25.00 a day; economy parking is $12.00 a day with free shuttles. Parking is first-come, first-served with no reservations.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi from Tampa International Airport?
faqs.a: Yellow Cab serves the airport from the Ground Transportation Areas Red 1 and Blue 2, outside baggage claim. The airport lists the fare as $3.50 for the first 1/5 mile plus $2.85 a mile, with a $22 minimum from the airport and a $40 flat rate to downtown Tampa and the cruise terminal.

faqs.q: How much does parking cost at Tampa International Airport?
faqs.a: The Short Term garage above the main terminal and the Long Term garage next to it charge nothing for the first hour, then $8 an hour, up to $32 and $26 per 24 hours. Economy Parking, linked by the SkyConnect train, is free for the first hour, then $5 an hour, up to $22 per 24 hours. Maximums include tax, stays are limited to 45 days, and the Cell Phone Waiting Lot is free.

faqs.q: Where do I pick up a rental car at Tampa International Airport?
faqs.a: At the Rental Car Center, reached by the SkyConnect train from the main terminal. Alamo, Avis, Budget, Dollar, Enterprise, Hertz, National, Thrifty, Ace, American, Fox, Payless, Sixt and Zipcar are there; off-airport companies pick up at the Rental Car Center's remote curb. Most domestic passengers can also check bags there from 5 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Where do I park for the St. Pete Pier?
faqs.a: The Pier's Dolphin and Pelican lots have more than 500 spaces; weekdays cost $2 an hour for the first four hours (six-hour maximum, $15) and weekends $2.50 an hour (six-hour maximum, $18). On Friday evenings and Saturday afternoons, when the lots fill, the Pier suggests the Sundial garage or the Al Lang lot, both within walking distance. The free Downtown Looper and Central Avenue Trolley also stop at the Pier.

faqs.q: How much is parking at St. Pete Beach and Pass-a-Grille?
faqs.a: The City of St. Pete Beach charges $5.00 an hour Monday through Thursday and $6.00 an hour Friday through Sunday, plus $1.00 an hour from February 1 to April 30. Pay by card at the pay stations (no cash), with the ParkMobile app, or by texting 'Park' to 77223. Pass-a-Grille Beach has 541 spaces on Gulf Way and 186 on Pass-a-Grille Way.

faqs.q: How much is beach parking on Treasure Island and Madeira Beach?
faqs.a: Treasure Island's city lots cost $5.00 an hour on weekdays and $5.50 on weekends and holidays ($6.00 and $6.50 on the Sunset Beach side streets); pay by text or with ParkMobile, and do not back into spaces, because license-plate readers enforce payment. Madeira Beach charges $4.00 an hour in its lots, paid through the ParkMobile app.

faqs.q: Is there a free shuttle on St. Pete Beach and Treasure Island?
faqs.a: Free Beach Ride runs an on-demand, door-to-door shuttle from the south tip of Pass-a-Grille to the northern parts of Madeira Beach. Call 727-776-7553, request a ride online or use its app when you are ready to go; it takes no advance bookings and does not go to the airports. Rides are free, and the operator says drivers welcome tips.

faqs.q: How much is the Jolley Trolley in Clearwater?
faqs.a: The Clearwater Jolley Trolley charges $2.25 a ride in cash (exact change) or $1.10 at the reduced rate, and children 8 and under ride free; contactless payment and group passes work through Flamingo Fares. Guests of the Sandpearl, Opal Sands, Sheraton Sand Key, Marriott Sand Key and TradeWinds ride free with their room card.

# getting-around: research report (Sep 27, 2026)

## What this slice covers
44 transport records, 33 FAQs (topic "Getting around") and 19 facts for visitors moving around Tampa Bay:

- **Airports (3):** Tampa International (TPA), St. Pete-Clearwater International (PIE), Sarasota Bradenton International (SRQ), with codes, addresses, points and ground transport. Plus TPA rideshare pickup, the TPA Rental Car Center (SkyConnect) and PIE rental cars.
- **Tampa transit:** TECO Line Streetcar (fare-free, hours, all 11 stations with HART's own GTFS coordinates, extension status), HART buses (Flamingo fares and caps, airport routes 10/30/32), DASH (the Tampa Downtown Partnership's $2 app-hailed service, which has replaced the Downtowner on the Partnership's pages), Pirate Water Taxi (10 stops as a route), and Lime/Spin e-scooters and e-bikes.
- **Pinellas transit:** PSTA buses (fares, caps, cash rules), SunRunner BRT, Route 100 and Route 300 express buses to Tampa and TPA, Central Avenue Trolley (free), Downtown Looper (free), Suncoast Beach Trolley, Jolley Trolley (beach and Coastal routes), Grouper Airport Express (PIE to Clearwater Beach), Clearwater Ferry, St. Pete Lime bike share and Spin/Lime scooters.
- **Across the bay:** the Tampa Bay Ferry (St. Pete-Tampa) is recorded as not running, with PSTA's Sep 2026 status.
- **Day trips:** Anna Maria Island Trolley (free, MCAT Route 5) and the Gulf Islands Ferry (Bradenton-Anna Maria).
- **Rail and intercity bus:** Amtrak at Tampa Union Station (the Floridian), Greyhound and FlixBus (Marion Transit Center and USF), RedCoach (USF).
- **Cruise:** Port Tampa Bay terminals 2, 3 and 6 with the five homeported lines, the garage and luggage rules.
- **Parking (6 records):** City of Tampa garages/meters, St. Pete downtown, Clearwater Beach, Pinellas County beach parks (new rates Oct 1 and Dec 1, 2026), Treasure Island, St. Pete Beach, plus PIE parking inside the PIE record.
- **Tolls (8):** SunPass, Toll-By-Plate, rental-car tolls, Selmon Expressway (THEA rate table), Veterans Expressway (with Suncoast Parkway in notes), Sunshine Skyway, Pinellas Bayway, Gateway Expressway (FDOT West Central Florida rate sheet, Apr 2026).

Counts by mode: airport 3, car-rental 2, rideshare 1, streetcar 1, bus 4, brt 1, trolley 5, microtransit 2, water-taxi 2, ferry 2, rail 1, intercity-bus 2, cruise-port 1, bike-share 1, scooter 2, parking 6, toll 8.
Counts by region (a record can list several): tampa 21, stpete 17, beaches 16, clearwater 13, around 6, daytrips 7. Every stop that names a place id points at a record that exists in another slice.

## How candidates were found
WebSearch was unavailable (the session's search budget was already used up by other agents), and Bing/DuckDuckGo scraping returned generic or captcha pages, so discovery ran through official sites and their own link structure:
Visit Tampa Bay's transportation page (visittampabay.com/stay/transportation/), the Tampa Downtown Partnership's Ways to Get Around page, the City of St. Petersburg's Transportation Options page, the City of Clearwater's Alternative Transportation page, PSTA's full route list (psta.net/rider-info/schedules-maps/), HART's schedules page and schedule book (Aug 16, 2026), HART's GTFS feed (gohart.org/google/google_transit.zip, version 2608.4: streetcar, SkyConnect and transit-center coordinates), Florida's Turnpike toll pages and the FDOT West Central Florida toll-rate PDF, the THEA site, fly2pie.com, the airport statistics PDF, Port Tampa Bay's cruise pages, and county/city parking pages. Pages were read with curl plus an HTML-to-text converter where sites allowed it, and with WebFetch where they did not (amtrak.com, greyhound.com, flixbus.com, redcoachusa.com, flysrq.com, myclearwater.com, stpetebeach.org); WebFetch-only facts are flagged in each record's notes. One WebFetch summary was caught being wrong (it said the Central Avenue Trolley runs every 22 minutes; the raw timetable shows every 30), so numbers were taken from raw text wherever possible.
